title: Cap a dry-erase marker: pull its cap off the back end, turn it round and push it onto the tip until it clicks
instruction: Take the cap off the back of the marker, put it on the tip until it clicks, and leave the capped marker lying on the table.
context: Capping a marker after writing, so it does not dry out, is something nearly everyone does at home, at school and at work. Here the cap starts posted on the back end, as it is left while writing. The robot must pull it off (about 1.2 N), turn it end for end, line it up over the 5 mm nib and push about 5 N along the marker, with the marker braced, until the snap ring inside the cap rides over the ridge on the barrel and clicks home, without the 7 g marker or the 2 g cap slipping or falling. Retention and click come from contact with sprung parts, not a joint switched on. The 'Cap and sort four pens' task was not accepted because its cap liner gave no resistance; the accepted lancing-device task snaps a cap on as one step, at 2 N; the accepted toothbrush task pushes a brush head on.
setup: Station table; one fixed layout as in the screenshot. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y to the left). Marker: one EXPO Low Odor chisel-tip dry-erase marker (item 80001, black), listed at 4.81 in (122 mm) long capped, 0.75 in (19 mm) across at its widest (the cap over its clip), 0.02 lb (9 g). Estimated details, to check with calipers: barrel black plastic, 15 mm across, 77 mm from its back end to its shoulder, 6.8 g; its last 10 mm narrower (12.3 mm) for posting the cap; in front of the shoulder a grey nose 11.7 mm across and 10 mm long with a snap ridge 12.6 mm across from 3.0 to 4.2 mm out, a 8 mm nib holder and a 5 x 2 mm chisel nib ending 30 mm in front of the shoulder. Cap: polypropylene, 45 mm long, 16.5 mm across, 2.2 g, bore 13 mm with a 0.6 mm lead-in, closed end 3 mm, a pocket clip 4 mm wide standing 2.5 mm proud from 12 to 44 mm in from the mouth; its snap ring stands 0.35 mm inside the ridge, so a cap pushed on rests on the ridge with its mouth about 3 mm out until a push of about 5 N clicks it home. Start: the cap is posted on the back end (its mouth against the step at the start of the narrow part, gripped there; pull-off about 1.2 N). The marker lies across the table (along y), resting on the cap and the barrel, tip toward the right arm, clip up: its shoulder at x 30, y -7 (nib's end at y -10), the cap's mouth at y -0.3 and its closed end at y 4.2. Both arms start in their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Scored every control step from the parts' poses; the score at the end of the trial counts. The cap is on the tip end when its axis is within 10 degrees of the marker's, pointing the same way as the tip, with the centre of its mouth within 2 mm of the marker's axis; the gap is the distance from the cap's mouth to the barrel's shoulder along the marker. 1.0: the cap is on the tip end with the gap 0.5 mm or less (clicked home), and the marker lies on the table (within 10 degrees of level; the lowest points of its back end and of the cap's closed end or clip within 3 mm of the table top), no part of either gripper is within 2 cm of the marker or the cap, and neither moved more than 1 mm over the preceding 1 s, all held together for 1 s (20 control steps in a row). Otherwise the best reached at any point: 0.8 on the tip end with the gap 0.5 mm or less; 0.6 on the tip end with the gap 4 mm or less (on the ridge, not clicked); 0.4 on the tip end with the gap 12 mm or less (the nib inside, the cap over the nose); 0.2 the cap pulled off the back end (the centre of the back end 5 mm or more outside the cap's mouth, or clear of its side); otherwise 0. Putting the cap back on the back end, reversed or beside the tip earns nothing more. In a real trial: the gap with a feeler gauge or calipers at the end and from the close video during the trial (the 16.5 mm cap as scale), the angles and the 2 cm by eye on the video, the ends' heights with a ruler.
reset_notes: Pull the cap off the tip, post it on the back end (push until it stops at the step), and lay the marker on its tape marks, clip up. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at the listed length, width and mass. Retention is contact: three 0.1 g rounded pads in the cap's mouth on preloaded radial springs (0.8 N, 2000 N/m; estimates: ~5 N click, ~1.2 N post pull-off) ride over a 0.45 mm ridge or grip the post; a real cap flexes a moulded ring. Barrel and cap are 16- and 12-sided so they lie still; the clip is a solid bar; the nib is rigid; ink drying is not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers reached the marker and turned it on the table; the cap stayed posted); demo: 1.0 (full score at step 1,846 of 2,400). Videos: overhead, left and right wrist cameras side by side.
